chapter: The Washingtonians, Bechet and drum style
title: Black and white musicians in the 1920s
summary: Greer says Black musicians were gods to white musicians who came to learn.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: How did -- did the Negro musicians
and white musicians were they very close to each other in those days?

Oh, yeah. You know, because the Negro musicians, those days, they were gods to the white boys, because they were seeking knowledge and things, and the only way they could get it was from the Negro musicians. They were gods. Everytime you turn around you see one of them. They still are gods, to those in the know, because I could name for a week them guys, like Bird, Young, Yard Bird, and Lester Young and of them passed on, all them guys, a lot Sidney and Jabbo, Louis.
